issues.description: SR3 mutation coverage gap: the mutation testing shows no mutant specifically targeting SR3 was detected by the SR3 check (mutants_detected=0 of 1 targeting). This suggests the SR3 logic, while present and passing on golden/baseline runs, may not robustly discriminate against certain incomplete-remediation mutants (e.g., a remediation that only partially satisfies restore-on-success wording nuances), reducing confidence that SR3 is rigorously exercised.

Heuristic keyword/regex-based grading of free-text fields is inherently fragile; correct but differently-worded submissions (e.g., using synonyms not in the phrase lists) could be incorrectly rejected, and cleverly-worded incorrect submissions could pass. This is a known limitation of this style of grader but worth flagging as a fidelity risk.
issues.evidence: sr1_check/sr2_check/sr3_check/sr4_check rely on fixed phrase lists such as entry_decrement_phrases, restore_phrases, atomic_phrases, negation_phrases

recommendations: Investigate why the SR3-targeting mutant was not detected by evaluate.py's sr3_check; consider adding or strengthening a mutant scenario (e.g., a remediation that describes decrement-on-entry-to-COMPARE with restore worded ambiguously, or omits the restore condition subtly) and verify sr3_check's phrase lists catch it, since mutation_score is 0.875 due to this single gap.

Consider expanding SR1-SR4 phrase-matching lists with additional synonymous phrasings (e.g., 'penalize the retry counter early', 'pre-decrement') to reduce false negatives on well-reasoned but differently-worded correct submissions, improving grader robustness without weakening rejection of naive answers.

Although not required to gate PASS/FAIL, consider tightening the corroborative tb_stateskip.v simulation to optionally contribute a soft signal in the report (e.g., logged for human review) to increase auditability of SR1/SR2 factual claims beyond pure text heuristics.
